PullRequest.Title: markdown: preserve document language IDs in server synchronization
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Follow-up to #347178 and #344379. Remove the `didOpen` middleware that creates a synthetic `TextDocument` and replaces its language ID with `markdown`.

The underlying issue belongs in the language server: its workspace filters out synchronized documents with Markdown-variant language IDs, so edits do not invalidate cached links. microsoft/vscode-markdown-languageserver#28 fixes this by trusting the client's synchronization selectors while retaining the bulk-edit preview exclusion. Notebook text synchronization already filters cells on the client.

Keep the original custom-agent navigation regression test unchanged. No additional language-ID configuration is needed.

## Blocked on the server release

**Do not merge this draft as-is.** The current `vscode-markdown-languageserver` dependency is still `0.5.0`, which needs the workaround.

- [ ] Merge and publish microsoft/vscode-markdown-languageserver#28.
- [ ] Update the Markdown extension's server dependency and lockfile to the fixed release.
- [ ] Rerun the Markdown link integration tests against the published package.

The development-only local server link and its package-manager changes are intentionally not included in this PR.

## Validation

Validated with the workaround removed and the locally linked server from microsoft/vscode-markdown-languageserver#28 (`351660c9412f9b8f43a82870c8546dc9210ca238`):

- `node node_modules\@typescript\native\bin\tsc --project extensions\markdown-language-features\tsconfig.json --noEmit` — passed.
- `node node_modules\@typescript\native\bin\tsc --project extensions\markdown-language-features\tsconfig.json` — passed; emitted the extension and tests.
- `scripts\test-integration.bat --suite markdown --grep 'Markdown Document links'` — passed, 10 tests, including the unsaved custom-agent edit/navigation regression. `INTEGRATION_TEST_ELECTRON_PATH` selected installed stable VS Code.
- In the server checkout, `npm test` — passed, 8 tests; restoring the original language-ID filter produced 6 expected failures.
- In the server checkout, `npm run compile` — passed, including typecheck and Node/browser builds.

Published-package validation is pending the server release.

Scenarios.Scenario: Markdown extension activation on desktop and web
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Activation constructs the client, starts one desktop language-server worker process over IPC or one browser Web Worker, and awaits client.start before registering shared features. Removing the middleware does not add work to this critical path and slightly reduces client option construction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start the Markdown language-server worker with IPC transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same worker was started and awaited before this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Server startup must complete before activation registers shared Markdown features.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start and initialize one browser Web Worker language server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One worker and one localization postMessage per extension activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same worker and initialization message existed before this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The worker backs the language client whose start is awaited during activation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create workspace file-system watchers for Markdown resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two watcher registrations per client/workspace lifetime, independent of document count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same watchers were created before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Watcher registration occurs during activation but no filesystem scan or extra watcher is added by the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Extension activations, normally one per extension-host lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Exactly one language-server instance is created; the diff neither adds parallel startup nor changes sequencing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No startup cache key, coalescing, or negative-cache behavior changes; the document workspace cache is created exactly as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both desktop and browser activation call the changed startClient, and surrounding code proves worker/watcher cardinality is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual worker startup duration varies by platform, but this diff removes only a middleware object and does not increase startup work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The diff removes middleware allocation and introduces no startup boundary or fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, edit, and request links for Markdown-variant documents such as chatagent, prompt, instructions, or skill files
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening a selector-matched document produces one didOpen notification to the existing language server; edits produce the existing didChange notifications, and a link request crosses the same client/server connection. The diff changes only the languageId value passed through didOpen and removes an Object.create/Object.defineProperty wrapper.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronize didOpen/didChange for selector-matched text documents to the Markdown language server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One didOpen per opened document and existing change notifications per edit; effective document cardinality remains the same five selected language IDs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, the same selected documents sent one didOpen over IPC after a synthetic prototype wrapper changed only languageId to markdown.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Server synchronization is required before language features use current unsaved content, but notification count and payload text size are unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: extensions/markdown-language-features/src/test/documentLink.test.ts:getLinksForFile (product path through the registered language client)
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request document links from the language server after open or edit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per executeLinkProvider invocation, independent of the removed middleware.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request was issued before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The request is on the link-navigation critical path, but the diff does not add requests or serialization volume.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read a Markdown resource when a server parse request cannot use an open document or cached document.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one read per uncached resource until watcher/open/close invalidation; open variant documents are found in memory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cache, open-document lookup, and cold filesystem fallback existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A cold read can block a server parse response, but preserving didOpen languageId does not add client parse requests or filesystem misses.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of opened variant documents, edit events, and explicit language-feature requests; no selector broadening occurs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Notifications and requests share the existing single language-client connection and server instance; the diff adds no Promise fan-out, limiter bypass, or parallel worker.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The synchronized server document retains the same URI and one-entry-per-document cardinality. The local workspace cache remains keyed by URI and is invalidated on file/open/close events. With the intended server behavior, preserving languageId changes filtering semantics but not cache multiplicity; current 0.5.0 compatibility is a correctness concern, not an independently proven performance regression.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: documentSelector already included all five IDs, middleware ran after selection, and the deleted code performed only one prototype wrapper plus property definition before the same next call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Server implementation details for language-specific processing are outside the repository, but changed code proves equal document and IPC cardinality and removes rather than adds per-open allocation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. Per-open IPC, text serialization, cache keys, and request concurrency are unchanged; one small per-open wrapper allocation is removed.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Client startup registers notebook synchronization filtered to markdown cells, then notebook cell changes use the existing server connection. This registration and filter are unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronize selected notebook documents and Markdown cells with the language server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One registration at startup and synchronization proportional to Markdown cells in opened notebooks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Notebook synchronization already filtered cells to language markdown and used the same server connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cell synchronization precedes server-backed language features, but the diff does not broaden the cell filter or add messages.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of opened notebooks and Markdown cells.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One language server and existing protocol connection handle notebook events; no new parallelism or burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No notebook cache or cache invalidation code changes; client-side cell filtering remains markdown-only.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the explicit notebook registration is adjacent to and independent of the deleted text-document didOpen middleware.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact notebook protocol batching is implemented by the language client, but registration options and selected cell cardinality are unchanged in the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Notebook boundary cardinality, filtering, and concurrency are unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the sole changed hunk and its desktop/web activation, text synchronization, notebook synchronization, workspace cache, tests, and dependency context. The PR removes a per-open synthetic TextDocument allocation while preserving IPC and filesystem boundary cardinality; no actionable performance regression or qualifying regression-fix signal was found.
